Settings.Name: Enable MIR
Settings.Description: Master switch. When off, MIR never rolls or injects anything.

Settings.Name: Base spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance that ANYTHING spawns at a looting opportunity (first stage of the two-stage roll), for every loot source that does not use its own chance (Loot Source Settings tab). Category shares decide WHAT spawns - set those on the MIR Browser tab.

Settings.Name: Rolls per looting opportunity
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per container/corpse, each at the spawn chance, for every loot source that does not use its own rolls (Loot Source Settings tab).

Settings.Name: Exclude the Nautiloid
Settings.Description: Never spawn anything during the Nautiloid prologue.

Settings.Name: Show item-received notification on spawn
Settings.Description: Use the game's item-received toast when MIR injects an item. Off = silent (items simply appear in the loot).

Settings.Name: Spawn in chests
Settings.Description: Roll on chests, strongboxes, coffers, sarcophagi, tombs, caskets, vaults, lockboxes and stashes. On by default. Chests can give anything in the pool. Off = MIR never rolls on chests; a chest you open while it is off is not marked, so it rolls the next time you open it after switching this back on. Your camp chest, tutorial chests and traveller's chests are never touched.

Settings.Name: Use its own chance and rolls
Settings.Description: Off = chests (chests, strongboxes, coffers, sarcophagi, tombs, caskets, vaults, lockboxes, stashes) use the spawn chance and rolls on the General tab. On = they use the two sliders below instead. The sliders start at 25% and 1 roll - the shipped General defaults, not whatever you have set on the General tab - so check them after ticking.

Settings.Name: Spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance per roll for chests (chests, strongboxes, coffers, sarcophagi, tombs, caskets, vaults, lockboxes, stashes) while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible and rolls once you raise it.

Settings.Name: Rolls
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per chest, each at the chance above, while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible.

Settings.Name: Spawn on corpses
Settings.Description: Roll when a corpse is first looted. Pre-placed bodies count; no combat required. Off = MIR never rolls on corpses.

Settings.Name: Use its own chance and rolls
Settings.Description: Off = corpses use the spawn chance and rolls on the General tab. On = they use the two sliders below instead. The sliders start at 25% and 1 roll - the shipped General defaults, not whatever you have set on the General tab - so check them after ticking.

Settings.Name: Spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance per roll for corpses while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible and rolls once you raise it.

Settings.Name: Rolls
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per corpse, each at the chance above, while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible.

Settings.Name: Spawn in barrels, crates and other clutter
Settings.Description: Roll on barrels, crates, sacks, baskets, trunks, pots and every other container that is not a chest, vase, wardrobe or bookshelf (the catch-all). Off by default. What they may give is set by the boxes below; with nothing ticked they give nothing.

Settings.Name: Barrels & crates: rings
Settings.Description: Modded rings (vanilla ones only with 'Include base-game items' on the Pool tab). Like all equipment, each ring can spawn only once per save, anywhere.

Settings.Name: Barrels & crates: potions
Settings.Description: Potions and elixirs - vanilla AND modded - even when the Pool tab's consumable settings are off. Admitted this way they appear in barrels and crates (and in the other of barrels / vases, if ticked there) ONLY - never in chests, on corpses, in wardrobes or in bookshelves. Consumables are never duplicate-limited.

Settings.Name: Barrels & crates: arrows
Settings.Description: Arrows - vanilla AND modded - on the same terms as potions above.

Settings.Name: Barrels & crates: alchemy ingredients
Settings.Description: Alchemy ingredients - vanilla AND modded - on the same terms as potions above. Ingredients ignore the rarity window (the game declares no rarity for them).

Settings.Name: Barrels & crates: everything
Settings.Description: Every category: equipment of all kinds, potions, arrows, ingredients, scrolls and camp clothing - the consumables, scrolls and camp clothing even when the Pool tab has them off (for barrels and crates only). The boxes above make no difference while this is ticked. Equipment drawn here comes from the same once-per-save pool as chests, and there are far more of these than chests.

Settings.Name: Use its own chance and rolls
Settings.Description: Off = barrels, crates and other clutter use the spawn chance and rolls on the General tab. On = they use the two sliders below instead. The sliders start at 25% and 1 roll - the shipped General defaults, not whatever you have set on the General tab - so check them after ticking.

Settings.Name: Spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance per roll for barrels, crates and other clutter while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible and rolls once you raise it.

Settings.Name: Rolls
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per container, each at the chance above, while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible.

Settings.Name: Spawn in vases, urns, jars and amphorae
Settings.Description: Roll on vases, urns, jars and amphorae (matched by name; pots are not vases, they stay with barrels). Off by default. What they may give is set by the boxes below; with nothing ticked they give nothing.

Settings.Name: Vases & urns: rings
Settings.Description: Modded rings (vanilla ones only with 'Include base-game items' on the Pool tab). Like all equipment, each ring can spawn only once per save, anywhere.

Settings.Name: Vases & urns: potions
Settings.Description: Potions and elixirs - vanilla AND modded - even when the Pool tab's consumable settings are off. Admitted this way they appear in vases and urns (and in the other of barrels / vases, if ticked there) ONLY - never in chests, on corpses, in wardrobes or in bookshelves. Consumables are never duplicate-limited.

Settings.Name: Vases & urns: arrows
Settings.Description: Arrows - vanilla AND modded - on the same terms as potions above.

Settings.Name: Vases & urns: alchemy ingredients
Settings.Description: Alchemy ingredients - vanilla AND modded - on the same terms as potions above. Ingredients ignore the rarity window (the game declares no rarity for them).

Settings.Name: Vases & urns: everything
Settings.Description: Every category: equipment of all kinds, potions, arrows, ingredients, scrolls and camp clothing - the consumables, scrolls and camp clothing even when the Pool tab has them off (for vases and urns only). The boxes above make no difference while this is ticked. Equipment drawn here comes from the same once-per-save pool as chests, and there are far more of these than chests.

Settings.Name: Use its own chance and rolls
Settings.Description: Off = vases, urns, jars and amphorae use the spawn chance and rolls on the General tab. On = they use the two sliders below instead. The sliders start at 25% and 1 roll - the shipped General defaults, not whatever you have set on the General tab - so check them after ticking.

Settings.Name: Spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance per roll for vases, urns, jars and amphorae while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible and rolls once you raise it.

Settings.Name: Rolls
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per container, each at the chance above, while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible.

Settings.Name: Spawn in wardrobes and closets
Settings.Description: Treat wardrobes and closets as their own loot source, filled with what you tick below. Your own camp wardrobe is never touched. Off = MIR ignores wardrobes entirely.

Settings.Name: Wardrobes: cosmetic clothes
Settings.Description: Allow camp clothing, camp shoes and underwear to spawn in wardrobes. This works even when 'Include cosmetics' on the Pool tab is off - a wardrobe setting decides what may appear IN A WARDROBE, and is not overruled by the pool-wide switch.

Settings.Name: Wardrobes: clothing and armour with stats
Settings.Description: Allow modded armour worn on the body - body armour, helmets, gloves, boots and cloaks - to spawn in wardrobes.

Settings.Name: Wardrobes: everything
Settings.Description: Every category - clothing and armour, weapons, shields, rings, amulets and camp clothing (whatever the Pool tab's cosmetics switch says). Consumables and scrolls only if the Pool tab includes them. The two boxes above make no difference while this is ticked. With NOTHING ticked, wardrobes give nothing (until v1.0.1 that meant anything).

Settings.Name: Use its own chance and rolls
Settings.Description: Off = wardrobes and closets use the spawn chance and rolls on the General tab. On = they use the two sliders below instead. The sliders start at 25% and 1 roll - the shipped General defaults, not whatever you have set on the General tab - so check them after ticking.

Settings.Name: Spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance per roll for wardrobes and closets while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible and rolls once you raise it.

Settings.Name: Rolls
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per wardrobe, each at the chance above, while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible.

Settings.Name: Spawn in bookshelves and desks
Settings.Description: Treat bookcases, bookshelves, book rows, stacks and piles, scroll shelves and desks as their own container class so they can be switched on separately and filled with scrolls rather than arrows. Off = MIR ignores them entirely. Name-matched, so apothecary and tailor desks count as desks and a scroll-shelf wine rack counts as a scroll shelf. Scroll detection is a heuristic (stat name, category or use type); a modded scroll that follows none of the vanilla conventions stays out of the pool.

Settings.Name: Bookshelves: scrolls
Settings.Description: Allow scrolls - vanilla and modded - to spawn in bookshelves. This works even when 'Include scrolls' on the Pool tab is off: a bookshelf setting decides what may appear IN A BOOKSHELF and is not overruled by the pool-wide switch. Scrolls admitted this way appear in bookshelves ONLY - never in chests, on corpses or in wardrobes (barrels and vases get scrolls only from their own 'everything' box). Unticking BOTH bookshelf content settings makes bookshelves spawn nothing at all. (With 'Include scrolls' on the Pool tab AND 'also spawn all other items' both on, scrolls are simply one of the pool-wide categories a bookshelf may draw, whatever this box says.)

Settings.Name: Bookshelves: also spawn all other items
Settings.Description: ADDS every other category - equipment, cosmetics and consumables, each subject to its own Pool setting - on top of scrolls. It does not replace them. With this on, scrolls compete with everything else in a bookshelf and their share slider on the MIR Browser tab becomes active; with it off, scrolls are the only thing a bookshelf can hold and the slider is inactive (100%).

Settings.Name: Use its own chance and rolls
Settings.Description: Off = bookshelves and desks use the spawn chance and rolls on the General tab. On = they use the two sliders below instead. The sliders start at 25% and 1 roll - the shipped General defaults, not whatever you have set on the General tab - so check them after ticking.

Settings.Name: Spawn chance (%)
Settings.Description: Chance per roll for bookshelves and desks while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible and rolls once you raise it.

Settings.Name: Rolls
Settings.Description: Independent attempts per bookshelf, each at the chance above, while 'Use its own chance and rolls' is ticked. 0 = never; anything passed over at 0 stays eligible.

Settings.Name: Include base-game items
Settings.Description: Let vanilla (non-modded) equipment enter the pool. Story and quest items are always hard-excluded.

Settings.Name: Include cosmetics
Settings.Description: Camp clothing, camp shoes and underwear categories, everywhere MIR rolls. Wardrobes (cosmetic clothes or everything) and barrels or vases on 'everything' admit them for themselves even while this is off.

Settings.Name: Include modded consumables
Settings.Description: Modded potions/elixirs, arrows and alchemy ingredients everywhere MIR rolls. Consumables are never duplicate-limited - they can drop repeatedly. Not needed for barrels or vases alone: their own potion, arrow and ingredient boxes (Loot Source Settings) admit them there by themselves.

Settings.Name: Include base-game consumables
Settings.Description: Vanilla potions/elixirs, arrows and alchemy ingredients EVERYWHERE MIR rolls (independent of the base-game items toggle). You do not need this for barrels or vases: their own boxes on the Loot Source Settings tab already admit vanilla consumables there, and only there.

Settings.Name: Include scrolls
Settings.Description: Let scrolls into the whole pool - chests, corpses, and wardrobes or bookshelves set to 'everything' / 'also spawn all other items'. (Barrels and vases get scrolls from their own 'everything' box, whatever this says.) ONE switch for vanilla AND modded scrolls, deliberately: it is not affected by 'Include base-game items' or by either consumables setting, so with it on you will find vanilla scrolls in chests even with base-game items off. Off (the default) does NOT stop bookshelves: 'Bookshelves: scrolls' admits them there on its own. Scrolls are consumables - they can drop repeatedly and are never duplicate-limited.

Settings.Name: Exclude known utility mods
Settings.Description: Keep items from known utility mods (photo-mode tools, cheat/tutorial-chest spawners, framework libraries) out of the pool. Recommended ON. Note: NPC/companion gear mods (starting-gear upgrades, NPC redesigns) are ALWAYS excluded and have no toggle - that gear belongs to its intended character.

Settings.Name: Excluded Mods
Settings.Description: ON: MIR skips three kinds of modded item. First, gear a mod puts on a specific NPC - that belongs to that character. Second, the mods on MIR's own list. Third, three containers on that same list, where the container and the items inside come from different mods, or where the container is the game's own furniture. Those last two kinds are rows on the Exclusions and overrides tab under 'Mods MIR does not use' - untick one there and MIR starts using it. NPC gear has no row and no toggle. Nothing else is skipped: a mod's own backpack, bag, box or chest counts as the mod handing the items to you, not as placing them in the world, so those items stay in MIR's pool and the mod still gives you its copy, which means you may end up with two. OFF: none of those three is skipped, including NPC gear, and duplicates are likelier. A mod you excluded yourself still applies either way. Either way this only ever stops MIR spawning a copy - it never removes anything the game or another mod gives you. Applies to modded equipment only: base-game items and consumables are never affected, and an item a quest mod spawns from its own script cannot be detected (exclude those by hand in the MIR Browser tab). Run !mir_tables in the server console for the full report of what is held back, what is not, and why.

Settings.Name: Limit rarity by level and Act
Settings.Description: Off (the default) = every rarity can spawn at every level and in every Act, which is how MIR has always behaved. On = the settings below apply. The rule that applies is the MOST RESTRICTIVE of your level band and your Act: the higher of the two minimums, and the LOWER of the two maximums. So lowering either one restricts the loot immediately. If a band and an Act do not overlap at all, MIR narrows to a single tier and says which two rules disagreed in the log. ALCHEMY INGREDIENTS IGNORE THIS WINDOW: the game declares no rarity for any ingredient, so they are all filed as Common and a window above Common would silently remove every one of them. Potions, arrows and scrolls do declare rarities and obey the window.

Settings.Name: Levels 1-5: lowest rarity
Settings.Description: The least valuable rarity MIR may spawn while your character is at levels 1-5. The rule that applies is the MOST RESTRICTIVE of your level band and your Act: the higher of the two minimums, and the LOWER of the two maximums. So lowering either one restricts the loot immediately. If a band and an Act do not overlap at all, MIR narrows to a single tier and says which two rules disagreed in the log. Alchemy ingredients ignore the window entirely (the game declares no rarity for them). Other items whose mod does not declare a rarity are filed as Common, and most cosmetic and clothing mods declare none - so setting a minimum above Common removes far more of the pool than you might expect. Run !mir_rarity to see how many items actually fall inside the window you have set.

Sections.SectionName: What MIR may and may not use

Settings.Name: Mods MIR does not use - untick one to let MIR use it
Settings.Description: TICKED means MIR does not spawn those items. Most rows are mods; three of them are containers, where the container and the items inside come from different mods, or where the container is the game's own furniture. UNTICK a row - or delete it with the X - and MIR starts using it from the next rebuild, which happens by itself while you are in a game, or at the next load if you change this from the main menu. Re-tick to skip it again. Unticking the box above the whole list lets MIR use all of its own suggestions at once - a mod you excluded yourself stays excluded - and re-ticking it brings every row back exactly as it was. MIR fills this list itself: its own suggestions start ticked - mods skipped because of the nature or the number of the items they include, such as hundreds of near-identical variants, or a container whose contents you would come across in the game anyway - and any mod you excluded yourself in the MIR Browser tab appears here too, also ticked. Typing a new name here does nothing; use the MIR Browser tab, which knows every mod's name. MIR's own rows here only matter while 'Excluded Mods' is ON (Pool tab); a mod you excluded yourself applies either way. MCM does not refresh an open list, so if you change your exclusions in the MIR Browser tab while this page is open, leave the tab and come back to see them.

Settings.Name: Show the advanced lists
Settings.Description: The list above works on whole MODS and is the one to use. Tick this to also show five more lists. Three work on INDIVIDUAL ITEMS - items MIR must never use, items you have let in even though their own mod places them, and odd items you want MIR to place in chests. The first of them is normally managed from the MIR Browser tab, which shows every item by name; in here it holds raw root-template UUIDs, so MCM is a fallback rather than the intended route. The other two are filled in here, or from the server console with !mir_forceinclude and !mir_extra: the Browser has no control for either. The other two are DISPLAY ONLY. One is the utility mods MIR is skipping, which simply follows 'Exclude known utility mods' on the Pool tab. The other is the NPC or companion gear, which has no toggle at all, because that gear belongs to its intended character. MCM draws a tick box above every list whether or not it does anything, and on those two it does nothing at all - MIR rewrites them immediately. Leave this unticked and nothing is lost.

Settings.Name: Items MIR must never use (checked = excluded)
Settings.Description: Root-template UUIDs of individual items that never enter the pool. Managed by the MIR Browser tab; editable here as a fallback.

Settings.Name: Items allowed in anyway (checked = allowed)
Settings.Description: Root-template UUIDs of items you have deliberately allowed into the pool even though their own mod already places them in the world. A DUPLICATE BECOMES POSSIBLE for each one: you may find the item where the mod puts it AND as MIR loot. Set here, or with !mir_forceinclude in the server console - the MIR Browser tab shows you which items are held back, but has no control to let one in. User exclusions still win. Has no effect while the placement filter on the Pool tab is off, because nothing is being fenced.

Settings.Name: Extra items MIR may place, in chests only
Settings.Description: Items MIR may hand out even though they are none of its usual categories - a modded consumable, a kit, an oddity. It can admit anything MIR does not already recognise; weapons and armour are already categories of their own, so they cannot be added here. They appear in CHESTS ONLY: never in barrels, vases, wardrobes, bookshelves or on corpses, whatever those sources allow. Write the item's STAT NAME exactly as it appears in the SPAWNED lines of MIR_log.txt (for example Goon_OBJ_Injury_Kit_B), or its root-template UUID. Each one spawns once per save, like equipment, and ignores the rarity window. An entry that is not in the pool is named in the log, with the reason. Empty by default. Console: !mir_extra add <name> / remove <name> / clear.

Settings.Name: Excluded mods - storage (not shown)
Settings.Description: Storage only, and hidden since v1.2.0: this is where your own per-mod exclusions are kept, as raw mod UUIDs. They are shown by NAME at the top of this tab under 'Mods MIR does not use', and in the MIR Browser tab, which is where to change them.

Settings.Name: Utility mods MIR is skipping - DISPLAY ONLY, these boxes do nothing
Settings.Description: DISPLAY ONLY. MIR's shipped utility-mod list, filtered to mods present in your load order. Checked = currently excluded (follows the 'Exclude known utility mods' toggle on the Pool tab). Ticking, unticking or Reset here has NO effect - the list refreshes itself automatically.

Settings.Name: NPC and companion gear MIR always skips - DISPLAY ONLY, these boxes do nothing
Settings.Description: DISPLAY ONLY. Gear meant for a specific NPC or companion (starting-gear upgrades, NPC redesigns) - permanently excluded, no toggle exists. Filtered to mods present in your load order. Ticking, unticking or Reset here has NO effect.

Settings.Name: MIR defaults you have switched off (storage)
Settings.Description: Storage only - set this at the top of the Exclusions and overrides tab. Holds the keys of MIR's own default exclusions you have turned off. A TICKED entry here means that default is OFF.

Settings.Name: Exclusion list prepared (storage)
Settings.Description: Storage only. Records that MIR has filled in the exclusion list once, including showing any inactive leftovers from the old raw list by name.

Settings.Name: Weapons
Settings.Description: Storage only - set this on the MIR Browser tab, which shows each category's live percentage beside its slider. Relative weight. A category's real probability is its weight divided by the sum of the weights of the categories it competes with in a given container type - live percentages and the ON / LIMITED / OFF status are on the MIR Browser tab. 0 disables the category.

Settings.Description: Storage only - set this on the MIR Browser tab, which shows each category's live percentage beside its slider. Relative weight. Settings.Name: Legacy: clutter consumables only (v1.0, not shown)
Settings.Description: Storage only. The v1.0 setting, replaced in v1.1 by the Barrels & crates boxes on the Loot Source Settings tab. Kept so MIR can tell you once, in its log, if you had it off. Changing it does nothing.

Settings.Name: Extra items
Settings.Description: Storage only - set this on the MIR Browser tab, which shows each category's live percentage beside its slider. Relative weight of the extra-items allow-list, which only chests can draw. 0 switches it off.
